models._description: Payment Provider (Toss Payments client/secret keys + computed webhook URL; KRW-only)
Payment Transaction (Toss Payments confirm/payments redirect flow; KRW)

security.note: No own ACL/rules; relies on payment's security and on base.group_system field groups guarding toss_payments_secret_key and toss_payments_payment_secret.

views.note: No own model views; xml_loc=55 is view inheritance (payment.provider form: Client Key / Secret Key (password) / Webhook URL (CopyClipboardChar) shown when code=='toss_payments') plus a QWeb inherit of payment.method_form injecting data-toss-payments-inline-form-values onto the payment radio via provider._toss_payments_get_inline_form_values, plus payment_provider_data.xml. No SDK <script> tag in XML: the Toss Payments v2 SDK is loaded at runtime by loadJS in payment_form.js.

behavioral_notes.observation: The outbound acquirer call (gap #7) is centralized through payment's payment.provider._send_api_request, which payment_toss_payments targets at https://api.tosspayments.com/ via the _build_request_url override (urljoin of host + endpoint), and authenticates with HTTP Basic auth via the _build_request_auth override returning (toss_payments_secret_key, '') -- the Toss 'secret_key:' Basic scheme (secret key as username, empty password). _build_request_headers adds an Idempotency-Key of '<orderId>:<paymentKey>' so the confirm POST is safe to retry. The one server-to-server call site is the success-return controller, which POSTs 'POST /v1/payments/confirm' with the redirect data (orderId, paymentKey, amount) to finalize the charge; _parse_response_error formats Toss's {message,code} body on failure. None of this server-to-server HTTP, the Basic secret-key scheme, or the idempotency key is visible in Python field/model metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: checkout / redirect flow: payment.transaction._get_specific_processing_values + payment_form.js (Toss v2 SDK requestPayment)
behavioral_notes.observation: Toss uses a hosted-window 'direct' redirect flow, not an inline charge. _get_specific_processing_values (override) returns order_name (=tx.reference), partner name/email/phone, and success_url (/payment/toss-payments/success) + fail_url (/payment/toss-payments/failure?access_token=<generated>) built from the base URL. On the browser side PaymentForm.prototype is patched (static/src/interactions/payment_form.js): _prepareInlineForm forces flow='direct'; _processDirectFlow loadJS('https://js.tosspayments.com/v2/standard'), reads the JSON inline-form values (client_key + Toss pm code via const.PAYMENT_METHODS_MAPPING card->CARD / bank_transfer->TRANSFER / mobile->MOBILE_PHONE) off the checked radio's data attribute, then TossPayments(clientKey).payment({customerKey: ANONYMOUS}).requestPayment({method, amount{currency:'KRW',value}, orderId=reference, orderName, successUrl, failUrl, customer*}) to open the Toss-hosted payment modal. _compute_reference is overridden to force a 'tx'-singularized alphanumeric/-/_ prefix because Toss rejects references with characters like INV/2025/. A sanitizeKoreanPhoneNumber helper validates the KR phone before passing it. This redirect/SDK orchestration is invisible to Python metadata (gap #3).

Three public routes (controllers/main.py). /payment/toss-payments/success (GET) locates the tx via payment.transaction._search_by_reference('toss_payments', data) (_extract_reference reads data['orderId']), runs _validate_amount({'totalAmount': data['amount']}) to defeat client-side amount tampering BEFORE confirming, and only if state!='error' POSTs /v1/payments/confirm and _process('toss_payments', payment_data) into payment's guarded state machine; on ValidationError it _set_error. /payment/toss-payments/failure (GET) verifies the request via payment_utils.check_access_token(access_token, reference) (an access token is used because the failure URL carries no paymentKey to confirm against the API) then _set_error('<message> (<code>)'). /payment/toss-payments/webhook (POST, csrf=False) parses get_json_data(), and for eventType in const.HANDLED_WEBHOOK_EVENTS ({'PAYMENT_STATUS_CHANGED'}) finds the tx and calls _verify_signature BEFORE _process. _verify_signature is a secret-equality check (not HMAC): unless status is in const.VERIFICATION_EXEMPT_STATUSES ({'EXPIRED','ABORTED'}) it hmac.compare_digest(received payment_data['secret'], tx.toss_payments_payment_secret) constant-time and raises werkzeug Forbidden on mismatch/missing. The per-payment 'secret' is captured into toss_payments_payment_secret during _apply_updates. Inbound state transitions and signature trust are invisible to metadata.

_apply_updates (override) stores provider_reference = payment_data['paymentKey'] and toss_payments_payment_secret = payment_data['secret'] (the webhook secret), then maps Toss status -> Odoo state via const.PAYMENT_STATUS_MAPPING {done:'DONE', canceled:'EXPIRED', error:'ABORTED'}: 'DONE' -> _set_done; 'EXPIRED' -> _set_canceled; a 'CANCELED'/'PARTIAL_CANCELED' status while already done is a no-op (refunds are NOT implemented, but Toss still webhooks on manual dashboard cancellations); anything else -> _set_error. _extract_amount_data forces currency_code='KRW' (const.SUPPORTED_CURRENCY) and amount=float(totalAmount). The provider is KRW-only: _get_supported_currencies filters to KRW and an @api.constrains rejects available_currency_ids other than base.KRW. This status->state semantics and the KRW-only guard are not derivable from field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: external integration surface (gap #7) -- endpoint, key, SDK
behavioral_notes.observation: Static gap-#7 facts (extract_frontend.py): uses_api_keys=true; one outbound endpoint -- https://api.tosspayments.com/ (direct REST, HTTP Basic secret-key auth, '/v1/payments/confirm') -- declared in models/payment_provider.py. No 'requests' import here: HTTP is delegated to payment.provider._send_api_request in the parent engine, which payment_toss_payments configures via the _build_request_url / _build_request_headers / _build_request_auth / _parse_response_error hook overrides. On the browser side the Toss Payments v2 'standard' SDK is loaded at runtime by loadJS('https://js.tosspayments.com/v2/standard') in payment_form.js (not a static <script> tag) -- a second, client-side channel to Toss for the hosted payment window. This dual server-to-server + client-side acquirer link is the canonical metadata gap #7: none of it is reachable from model/field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (static) -- Toss Payments inline form patch
behavioral_notes.observation: 1 JS file, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds (gap #3). The module patches one shared payment widget rather than registering new components: PaymentForm.prototype (static/src/interactions/payment_form.js) forces the 'direct' flow and drives the Toss Payments v2 SDK hosted payment window from the inline-form values JSON produced by payment.provider._toss_payments_get_inline_form_values (client_key + mapped pm code), injected onto the checkout radio by a QWeb inherit of payment.method_form. Assets load into web.assets_frontend (manifest glob static/src/**/*). These browser interactions and the Toss SDK are invisible to Python metadata (gap #3).

external_integrations.sdk: Toss Payments v2 'standard' JS SDK (browser hosted-window, loadJS at runtime); server side uses no python SDK -- HTTP via payment.provider._send_api_request
external_integrations.auth: HTTP Basic with toss_payments_secret_key as username and empty password (Toss 'secret_key:' scheme), Idempotency-Key header
external_integrations.pattern: Concrete realization of metadata gap #7: a real external acquirer integration covering the South Korea market. Outbound server-to-server REST to api.tosspayments.com (POST /v1/payments/confirm) authenticated with the secret key via HTTP Basic auth and an Idempotency-Key; a parallel client-side Toss v2 SDK channel that opens the hosted payment window (card / bank transfer / mobile, KRW only); and inbound settlement via a redirect success/failure pair plus a PAYMENT_STATUS_CHANGED webhook whose authenticity is a constant-time secret-equality compare against the per-payment secret. The base 'payment' engine flags uses_api_keys but ships no live acquirer -- this module is exactly that override.
external_integrations.note: Prime gap-#7 example: none of the Toss endpoint, the Basic secret-key auth, the webhook secret trust, or the browser SDK channel are derivable from Python model/field metadata; they were established only by reading models/payment_provider.py + payment_transaction.py + controllers/main.py + const.py.

capabilities: Accept Online Payments via Toss Payments (hosted-window direct flow, South Korea)
Card / Bank Transfer / Mobile-phone payment methods (KRW only)
Asynchronous settlement via secret-verified PAYMENT_STATUS_CHANGED webhook
Idempotent payment confirmation (Idempotency-Key on the confirm POST)
value_streams: Collect-Payment (Toss): initiate tx -> Toss v2 SDK requestPayment hosted window -> redirect /payment/toss-payments/success -> _validate_amount -> POST /v1/payments/confirm (api.tosspayments.com) -> _process -> state machine done/error -> downstream post-process settlement; OR async /payment/toss-payments/webhook (PAYMENT_STATUS_CHANGED, secret-verified) -> _process
information_concepts: payment.provider (Toss credentials: client key / secret key / computed webhook URL)
payment.transaction (mapped to a Toss payment: orderId=reference, paymentKey=provider_reference, per-payment secret)
organization: (no module-owned res.groups; toss_payments_secret_key and toss_payments_payment_secret are restricted to base.group_system; everything else inherits payment's groups/record rules)
policies: KRW only: _get_supported_currencies filters to KRW and an @api.constrains rejects available_currency_ids other than base.KRW (ValidationError)
Amount integrity: the success-return route runs _validate_amount on the redirected amount before confirming the payment, defeating client-side amount tampering

Webhook authenticity: PAYMENT_STATUS_CHANGED events must pass _verify_signature (constant-time compare of payment_data['secret'] vs tx.toss_payments_payment_secret) or are rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden; EXPIRED/ABORTED statuses are verification-exempt
Failure-return authenticity: the failure URL carries a generated access_token verified via check_access_token (no paymentKey to confirm against the API)
Idempotency-Key (orderId:paymentKey) sent on the confirm POST so the charge is safe to retry
References forced to a 'tx'-singularized alphanumeric/-/_ prefix to satisfy Toss reference rules
Secret/webhook keys gated by base.group_system field groups
stakeholders: Merchant / Company (res.company, holds the Toss account & keys)
Toss Payments (external acquirer / PSP, South Korea)
Accountant (consumes settled payments via account_payment downstream)
metrics: (no own reports; transaction volumes/amounts/state surfaced by the parent payment.transaction pivot/graph)

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.5 process payments / collect cash; manage external payment provider)
classification.rationale: payment_toss_payments is a value-NETWORK (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating-technology) component: a concrete acquirer adapter whose purpose is to interconnect two parties who would not otherwise transact directly -- the South-Korean payer and the merchant -- by linking the merchant to Toss Payments' card / bank-transfer / mobile network. It exhibits the mediating-technology activities: network promotion & contract management (provider credential/key management, webhook URL provisioning, KRW/reference constraints), service provisioning (opening the Toss hosted payment window and confirming the charge per transaction via /v1/payments/confirm), and infrastructure operation (the server-to-server api.tosspayments.com link, the Toss v2 SDK client channel, and the redirect + signed-webhook settlement loop). It does not transform inputs into outputs (chain) nor solve a bespoke customer problem (shop). It inherits the parent 'payment' engine's value_model exactly: the engine is the generic mediator and this module is its Toss realization. activity_class is 'support' because, from the enterprise value-chain perspective, payment acceptance is an infrastructure/finance support function (category Accounting/Payment Providers, application=False, no end-user app) sitting under 9.0 Manage Financial Resources -- specifically 9.5 process payments / collect cash, with the side of 'manage an external payment provider'. So value_model=network (its own internal logic is mediation, an acquirer integration -- gap #7), activity_class=support (its place on the enterprise value chain). This mirrors the parent payment.metamodel.json (network/support) and the payment_stripe sibling (network/support).

standard_capabilities: direct hosted-window online payment via the Toss Payments v2 SDK (card / bank transfer / mobile)
server-side payment confirmation with amount validation against tampering (POST /v1/payments/confirm)
asynchronous settlement via a PAYMENT_STATUS_CHANGED webhook plus redirect success/failure routes
idempotent confirm requests (Idempotency-Key) and KRW-only currency enforcement
secret-key HTTP Basic authentication of all outbound calls
typical_fits: South-Korea online shop / portal checkout collecting KRW card / bank-transfer / mobile payments through Toss
send-a-payment-link or pay-an-invoice-online collection (with account_payment / sale downstream)
single-currency (KRW) merchant acceptance with the Toss-hosted payment window
common_gaps: refunds are explicitly NOT implemented (CANCELED/PARTIAL_CANCELED webhooks on a done tx are no-ops; cancellation done on the Toss merchant dashboard)
tokenization / saved cards are not implemented (no payment.token override; customerKey is ANONYMOUS)
manual capture / authorize-then-capture / void are not implemented (hosted direct flow only)
single currency only: KRW is enforced by constraint, so multi-currency acceptance is impossible
the public-URL requirement for the webhook means local/dev instances need a tunnel for async status updates
bespoke reconciliation / settlement document chains live downstream (account_payment, sale), not here

Real-world distribution of Toss transaction states and payment-method split (card vs bank transfer vs mobile); no runtime row counts captured.
Whether refund / cancellation will be added (currently dashboard-only) and how it would map to child payment.transaction records.
Which downstream modules consume the settled Toss transactions (account_payment, sale) and how KRW (zero-decimal currency) amounts flow.
